components.statement: Zscaler provides a predefined URL filtering rule (CIPA Compliance Rule) and a control (Enable CIPA Compliance) to enable the predefined rule, and a CIPA Compliance Report with insights into the traffic and users blocked from accessing the prohibited content based on the rule. The rule is activated by enabling the Enable CIPA Compliance option from Data Security > Inline CASB > Advanced Policy Settings.

quotes: Zscaler provides a predefined URL filtering rule (CIPA Compliance Rule) and a control (Enable CIPA Compliance) to enable the predefined rule.
It also provides a CIPA Compliance Report which gives insights into the traffic and users that are blocked from accessing the prohibited content based on the CIPA Compliance Rule.
To activate the CIPA Compliance Rule, enable the Enable CIPA Compliance option from the Data Security > Inline CASB > Advanced Policy Settings.

enable-conditions.statement: The page says the Enable CIPA Compliance option cannot be enabled when: the number of URL filtering policy rules exceeds the limit; a rule with rule order 1 exists with a higher admin rank; the CIPA Compliance Rule is activated under Internet Access > Policy > URL Filtering; and the Advanced URL Filtering Options Enable Suspicious New Domains Lookup, Enable AI/ML-based Content Categorization, Enable Embedded Sites Categorization and Enforce SafeSearch are enabled. After the last group the page says "You cannot disable the following options".

quotes: You cannot enable the Enable CIPA Compliance option when:
The number of URL filtering policy rules exceeds the limit.
A rule with rule order 1 exists with a higher admin rank.
The CIPA Compliance Rule is activated under Internet Access > Policy > URL Filtering.
The following Advanced URL Filtering Options under Data Security > Inline CASB > Advanced Policy Settings are enabled. You cannot disable the following options:
Enable Suspicious New Domains Lookup
Enable AI/ML-based Content Categorization
Enable Embedded Sites Categorization
Enforce SafeSearch

first-activation.statement: When the CIPA Compliance Rule is activated for the first time, it takes the highest precedence (rule order 1) by default and the rule order is automatically incremented by 1 for the other rules. If the logged-in user does not have an admin rank, the rule is created with an admin rank 7. No custom URL filtering rule can be created with the name CIPA Compliance Rule.

quotes: When the CIPA Compliance Rule is activated for the first time, it takes the highest precedence (rule order 1) by default. The rule order is automatically incremented by 1 for the other rules.
If the logged-in user does not have an admin rank, then the rule is created with an admin rank 7.
You cannot create any custom URL filtering rule with the name CIPA Compliance Rule.

disable-behavior.statement: When Enable CIPA Compliance is disabled, the CIPA Compliance Rule gets disabled under Internet Access > Policy > URL Filtering but the disabled rule can still be viewed, and the Advanced URL Filtering Options are set to the recommended policy settings. The rule can be viewed once the Enable CIPA Compliance option has been selected at least once, and it can be deleted only when the Enable CIPA Compliance toggle is disabled.

quotes: When you disable the Enable CIPA Compliance option, a warning message appears
The CIPA Compliance Rule gets disabled under Internet Access > Policy > URL Filtering. However, you can view the disabled rule.
The Advanced URL Filtering Options under the Data Security > Inline CASB > Advanced Policy Settings are set to the recommended policy settings.
You can view the CIPA Compliance Rule under Internet Access > Policy > URL Filtering if you select the Enable CIPA Compliance option at least once.
You can delete the CIPA Compliance Rule only when you disable the Enable CIPA Compliance toggle.

rule-categories.statement: The rule's URL categories are all the predefined categories under the URL super category Legal Liabilities, with predefined URLs and keywords, from Adult Sex Education to Weapons/Bombs in the page's list; the custom categories under Legal Liabilities are excluded. URL categories cannot be added to or deleted from the predefined list, but custom URLs and keywords (CIPA related) can be added or deleted in any predefined category under Legal Liabilities.

quotes: List of all the predefined categories under the URL super category, Legal Liabilities with predefined URLs and keywords. The custom categories under Legal Liabilities are excluded.
You cannot add or delete URL categories from the predefined list. However, you can add or delete custom URLs and keywords (CIPA related) from any predefined category under Legal Liabilities.

Adult Sex Education, Adult Themes, Alcohol/Tobacco, Anonymizer, Computer Hacking, Copyright Infringement, Drugs, Gambling, K-12 Sex Education, Lingerie/Bikini, Mature Humor, Militancy/Hate and Extremism

Newly Registered and Observed Domains, Nudity, Other Adult Material, Other Illegal or Questionable, Pornography, Profanity, Questionable, Body Art, Social Networking Adult, Tasteless, Violence, Weapons/Bombs

fixed-attributes.statement: The rule's request methods are listed as OPTIONS, GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, TRACE, CONNECT, OTHER and ALL. The page marks these attributes Non-editable: applicable to all users, groups, departments, locations and location groups in the organization, applicable at any time and to all protocols, access denied to all the sites that fall under the specified URL categories, no exception allowed for the blocked sites, and no redirect URL configured.

quotes: OPTIONS, GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, TRACE, CONNECT, OTHER, ALL
(Non-editable) Applicable to all the users in the organization.
(Non-editable) Applicable to all the groups in the organization.
(Non-editable) Applicable to all the departments in the organization.
(Non-editable) Applicable to all the locations of the organization.
(Non-editable) Applicable to all the location groups of the organization.
(Non-editable) Applicable at any time.

(Non-editable) Access is denied to all the sites that fall under the specified URL categories.

report-location.statement: The CIPA Compliance Report is viewed on the Standard Reports tab, in the Liability Exposure section, and can be scheduled by selecting CIPA Compliance Report as the Report in the Add Scheduled Report window.

quotes: On the Standard Reports tab, go to the Liability Exposure section to view the report.
In the Add Scheduled Report window, for Report, select CIPA Compliance Report, and configure the rest of the window.

rule-count-limit.title: What "exceeds the limit" means for the URL Filtering rule count
rule-count-limit.detail: The page lists the number of URL filtering policy rules exceeding the limit as a condition, without stating the limit or how much headroom the rule needs.

disable-warning-text.title: What warning appears when Enable CIPA Compliance is disabled
disable-warning-text.detail: The capture's text on the disabling warning reads "a warning message appears and we can add an image. You can get the image in beta", which does not give the warning text.

api-representation.title: How the CIPA option is represented in the API
api-representation.detail: The API field that the SDK checks (enableCipaCompliance) is outside the captured article.
